Clinical History: 30-year-old female with an abnormal Pap test result of Low-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (LSIL) and positive for high-risk HPV.
Diagnosis: Cervix, 6 o'clock, Biopsy: High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (CIN 2).
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled "cervix 6 o'clock," are two fragments of tan-white mucosal tissue, each measuring approximately 0.3 cm. Submitted entirely in one cassette.
Microscopic Description: Sections show squamous mucosa with marked architectural disorganization. There is a proliferation of atypical basaloid cells extending into the middle third of the epithelial thickness. These cells exhibit enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei with irregular contours and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Mitotic figures are noted above the basal layer. The stromal-epithelial junction is well-defined.
Comment: The findings are diagnostic of CIN 2, a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion. Correlation with colposcopic findings and appropriate clinical management is advised.

Specimen: Cervical biopsy at 6 o'clock
Pathologist: Dr. Mark Jennings

Report status: Final

Clinical History: 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus nephritis.

Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)

Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.

Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
Fibrinogen: Negative.
Albumin: Negative.

Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells.
There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.

Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A).

Pathologist: Dr. Richard Lee

Specimen: Native kidney biopsy
Report status: Final

Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma.
Diagnosis: Lymph Node, Left Cervical. Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis
Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass'; is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance. Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD15: Positive
PAX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
Specimen: Left cervical lymph node
Report status: Final
Pathologist: Dr. Benjamin Ayers

V).
Specimen Adequacy: The specimen is adequate for evaluation.
Microscopic Description: The aspirate is cellular and shows crowded clusters of follicular cells with
microfollicular architecture. The cells exhibit nuclear enlargement, chromatin pallor, and irregular
nuclear contours. Occasional nuclear grooves and rare intranuclear cytoplasmic pseudoinclusions are
identified. Colloid is scant in the background. The features are highly suspicious for Papillary Thyroid
Carcinoma.
Comment: The cytomorphologic features are suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma. Per the
Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology, surgical excision is recommended for definitive
diagnosis.

The patient is a 22-year-old male who presented for a routine skin examination.
He noted a mole on his upper back that he believes has become slightly darker
over the past year. He denies any symptoms of pain or itching associated with the
lesion. He has a history of significant sun exposure during his teenage years and
reports occasional sunburns.
PROCEDURES:
Shave Biopsy, Upper Back: A 5mm pigmented macule was identified on the
superior aspect of the right scapula. After obtaining consent, the area was
anesthetized with 1% lidocaine with epinephrine, and a deep shave biopsy of the
lesion was performed. Hemostasis was achieved with aluminum chloride. The
specimen was sent for histopathologic examination.
IMPRESSION:
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION: Sections show a symmetric, well-circumscribed
proliferation of nested and single melanocytes confined to the dermal-epidermal
junction. The melanocytes are uniform in size and shape with no significant
cytologic atypia. No mitotic activity or ulceration is identified.
DIAGNOSIS: Junctional melanocytic nevus, benign.
